title: 2025年6月四级真题 第1套 阅读1
paperTitle: 2025年6月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
passage:
P1 New research suggests that pandas may be at risk of dying out because they are too comfortable. Experts say too much happiness can stop the bears from searching for new mates.

P2 Environmentalists have long believed that building roads or homes near the bears may threaten their survival by "reducing or fragmenting their natural: habitats", The Times reported. But the new research suggests that a "modest degree of discomfort and fragmentation" may actually help preserve panda populations.

P3 The research was conducted by scientists from Michigan State University. It concluded that pandas fail to wander off in search of new mates if they find their habitat too comfortable, resulting in a lack of vital genetic diversity.

P4 For their study—outlined in a paper in the journal Conservation Biology—the team looked at genetic diversity and spread among a Chinese panda population. The ideal level of perfectly livable habitat was found to be only 80% of an area, with the remainder either too harsh or too affected by human activity.

P5 The experts concluded that pandas should ideally "be happy enough to thrive, but not so content that they don't want to move around and find new mates".

P6 Their conclusions about what The Guardian described as this "sweet spot" are in line with the so-called Goldilocks principle: that there can be just the right amount of something. The concept has been applied to a wide range of disciplines, from developmental psychology to economics and engineering.

P7 Claudio Sillero, a professor of conservation biology at Oxford University, told the newspaper that the new findings could have implications beyond panda conservation.

P8 "Most large animals that eat meat live in increasingly fragmented landscapes," said Sillero, who was not involved in the research. "It may well be that the messy nature of their relationship with human efforts induces more animals to scatter or travel further, and might result in greater genetic connectivity and enhanced population persistence."

P9 The most recent count of pandas found that there were more than 1,800 left in the wild, putting them on the list of vulnerable, but not endangered, species.

questions.q: What do we learn from new research about pandas?
options: They are losing habitat due to the building of roads and houses.
They have stopped seeking new mates for reproduction.
They may not adapt to the fragmentation of their habitat.
They may cease to exist as a result of enjoying too good a life.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn from new research about pandas? 问 "new research" 直接告诉了我 们什么，是对研究结论原文的客观转述题。

【拆句】题干 Q46 是一个标准 wh- 问句：What 作 learn 的宾语，from new research 是来源状 语，about pandas 修饰 research，限定研究对象。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】New research suggests that pandas may be at risk of dying out because they are too comfortable. 新的研究表明，熊猫可能因为生活得太舒适而面临灭绝的风险。

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 losing habitat due to the building of roads and houses 是 P2 中 environmentalists "long believed" 的旧观点，并非新研究的结论。 B) 过度推断 原文是 pandas fail to wander off in search of new mates if they find their habitat too comfortable——条件状语限定，They have stopped seeking new mates for reproduction. 删掉条件、把可能性说成全体熊猫已经停止寻偶，与原文不符。 C) 与原文相反 新研究主张栖息地适度碎片化反而"helps preserve"熊猫，They may not adapt to the fragmentation of their habitat. 反过来说熊猫不能适应碎片化，与原文相反。 D) ✓ 正确 may be at risk of dying out ↔may cease to exist because they are too comfortable ↔as a result of enjoying too good a life D 选项把"太舒适 → 可能灭绝"两层语义都对位地复述了一遍，与预判完全等值，可直接 锁定。 46. What do we learn from new research about pandas? A) They are losing habitat due to the building of roads and houses. B) They have stopped seeking new mates for reproduction. C) They may not adapt to the fragmentation of their habitat. D) They may cease to exist as a result of enjoying too good a life. 从Michigan State University科学家的新研究中我们可以得出什么结论? A) 环保主义者关于熊猫保护的长期观点可能具有误导性。 B) 熊猫栖息地附近的住宅开发可能威胁到它们的生存。 C) 熊猫的自然栖息地正变得越来越不适合繁殖。 D) 熊猫数量的增加归因于它们栖息地的破碎化。

questions.q: What can we conclude from the new research by scientists at Michigan State University?
options: Environmentalists' long-time belief regarding panda conservation may be misleading.
Housing development near pandas' homes may threaten their survival.
Pandas' natural habitats are becoming less suitable for reproduction.
The increased panda population is attributed to the fragmentation of their habitat.
questions.explain:
【判型】What can we conclude from the new research 中的 conclude 是推断/结论类信号词， 要求在原文事实之上做一步合理推导。

【拆句】What can we conclude from the new research by scientists at Michigan State University? 中 by scientists at Michigan State University 是介词短语后置修饰 research，限定研究来源；主干 What can we conclude 即 "我们可以得出什么结论"，结 构简单。

【定位】The research was conducted by scientists from Michigan State University. It concluded that pandas fail to wander off in search of new mates if they find their habitat too comfortable, resulting in a lack of vital genetic diversity. 这项研究由密歇根州立大学的科学家们开展。研究得出结论：如果熊猫觉得栖息地太舒服， 它们就不会外出寻找新的配偶，从而导致缺乏关键的遗传多样性。 47. What can we conclude from the new research by scientists at Michigan State University? A) Environmentalists' long-time belief regarding panda conservation may be misleading. B) Housing development near pandas' homes may threaten their survival. C) Pandas' natural habitats are becoming less suitable for reproduction. D) The increased panda population is attributed to the fragmentation of their habitat.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 Environmentalists have long believed that building roads or homes near the bears may threaten their survival ↔Environmentalists' long-time belief regarding panda conservation But the new research suggests that a modest degree of discomfort and fragmentation may actually help preserve panda populations. ↔may be misleading A 项正是把 P2 的"旧信念"与 P3 新研究的反向结论合在一起得出的合理推断，与预判完 全一致。 B) 张冠李戴 Housing development near pandas' homes may threaten their survival. 几乎是 P2 旧观点的原文转述，不是新研究的结论。 C) 无中生有 原文只说舒适让熊猫不愿外出找新伴，未说栖息地"不适合繁衍"；Pandas' natural habitats are becoming less suitable for reproduction. 是无中生有。 D) 与原文相反 原文是"栖息地碎片化"对熊猫"种群延续"有帮助，而非"碎片化使熊猫数量增加"。The increased panda population is attributed to the fragmentation of their habitat. 把 帮助保存说成数量增加，且因果说法不准确，与原文相反。 专家们关于熊猫的结论是什么? A) 为它们提供理想的栖息地以便繁衍生息是紧迫的。 B) 保护它们的遗传多样性非常重要。 C) 它们找到新配偶的机会与它们的栖息地有很大关系。 D) 它们的生存环境一直在持续恶化。

questions.q: What is the experts' conclusion regarding pandas?
options: It is urgent to provide an ideal habitat for them to thrive.
It is very important to preserve their genetic diversity.
Their chances of finding new mates have a lot to do with their habitat.
Their environment for survival has been continuously worsening.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is the experts' conclusion regarding pandas? 问专家给出的明确结论，是对一段 原文的客观复述。

【拆句】What is the experts' conclusion regarding pandas? 中 regarding pandas 是介词短 语作 conclusion 的修饰语，相当于 about pandas，限定结论的对象；句子是简单系表 结构。

【定位】The experts concluded that pandas should ideally "be happy enough to thrive, but not so content that they don't want to move around and find new mates". 专家们得出结论：熊猫理想的状态应当是"既能开心地繁衍生息，又不至于舒服到不愿四处 走动去寻找新的配偶"。 48. What is the experts' conclusion regarding pandas? A) It is urgent to provide an ideal habitat for them to thrive. B) It is very important to preserve their genetic diversity. C) Their chances of finding new mates have a lot to do with their habitat. D) Their environment for survival has been continuously worsening.

【选项】A) 无中生有 P5 强调的是"恰好的舒适度"，不是"提供一个理想的栖息地刻不容缓"。It is urgent to provide an ideal habitat for them to thrive. 中 urgent 是原文未提的紧迫态度，且 ideal habitat 把原文复杂的"sweet spot"过度简化。 B) 张冠李戴 遗传多样性出现在 P3 是机制说明，不是 P5 专家结论的内容。It is very important to preserve their genetic diversity. 直接把别处的细节当作"专家结论"。 C) ✓ 正确 be happy enough to thrive, but not so content that they don't want to move around and find new mates ↔Their chances of finding new mates have a lot to do with their habitat. their habitat（隐含于 happy/content 之中——"舒适"是栖息地状态）↔their habitat C 用"栖息地与找新伴几率有关"概括了预判中的两层逻辑，且未做超出原文的推论，是 最贴的概括项。 D) 无中生有 原文只在 P2 提到旧观点中道路住宅可能威胁栖息地，但新研究并未说生存环境"持续在 恶化"。Their environment for survival has been continuously worsening. 是无中 生有。 从文章中我们可以推断出关于Goldilocks原则的什么信息? A) 它需要通过更多关于熊猫的研究来证实。 B) 它也适用于熊猫的保护。 C) 它对未来的熊猫研究具有启示意义。 D) 它可以用来定位熊猫的合适地点。

questions.q: What can we infer from the passage about the Goldilocks principle?
options: It needs to be confirmed by more studies on pandas.
It applies to the preservation of pandas too.
It has implications for future panda research.
It can be used to locate the right spot for pandas.
questions.explain:
【判型】What can we infer from the passage 中 infer 是推断题的标志词，要求基于原文做一步合 理推导。

【拆句】What can we infer from the passage about the Goldilocks principle?：about the Goldilocks principle 是介词短语，作 infer 的宾语补足说明，相当于 "关于 Goldilocks 原 则"。结构无陷阱。

【定位】Their conclusions about what The Guardian described as this "sweet spot" are in line with the so-called Goldilocks principle: that there can be just the right amount of something. 他们关于《卫报》所说的这个"甜点位"的结论，与所谓的 Goldilocks 原则一致：即任何事 物都可以有一个恰到好处的量。 49. What can we infer from the passage about the Goldilocks principle? A) It needs to be confirmed by more studies on pandas. B) It applies to the preservation of pandas too. C) It has implications for future panda research. D) It can be used to locate the right spot for pandas.

【选项】A) 无中生有 It needs to be confirmed by more studies on pandas. 原文未提及；Goldilocks 原 则是"被沿用"的概念，不存在"还需进一步研究确认"的语义。 B) ✓ 正确 Their conclusions about what The Guardian described as this "sweet spot" are in line with the so-called Goldilocks principle ↔It applies to the preservation of pandas too. applied to a wide range of disciplines, from developmental psychology to economics and engineering ↔applies to … too B 用 applies to … too 精确表达了"该原则同样适用于熊猫保护"，是 in line with 一步 推出的合理结论。 C) 与原文相反 原文是熊猫研究印证了原则，不是原则对熊猫研究有启示。It has implications for future panda research. 把作用方向反着写。 D) 偷换概念 It can be used to locate the right spot for pandas. 把 sweet spot 误当成熊猫的地理 sweet spot；原文的 sweet spot 是"恰好的舒适程度"的比喻，不是物理位置。 根据Sillero教授的说法,新发现能够做什么? A) 有助于发现保护熊猫的新方法。 B) 有助于将熊猫从濒危物种名单中移除。 C) 为大多数大型食肉动物的保护提供启示。 D) 展示人类与动物之间互动的复杂性。

questions.q: What can the new findings do according to Professor Sillero?
options: Help discover new ways for the conservation of pandas.
Help remove pandas from the list of endangered species.
Shed light on the conservation of most large meat-eating animals.
Show the complexity of interactions between humans and animals.
questions.explain:
【判型】What can the new findings do according to Professor Sillero? 直接问 Sillero 教授的原 话，是对引语原文的客观转述。

【拆句】What can the new findings do according to Professor Sillero? 主干是 What can the new findings do，according to Professor Sillero 是介词短语作来源状语；句中 do 是实 义动词，被 What 提前作宾语。

【定位】It may well be that the messy nature of their relationship with human efforts induces more animals to scatter or travel further, and might result in greater genetic connectivity and enhanced population persistence. 很可能正是它们与人类活动这种"乱糟糟"的关系，促使更多动物分散、走得更远，从而带来 更强的遗传连通性，以及种群存续能力的提升。 50. What can the new findings do according to Professor Sillero? A) Help discover new ways for the conservation of pandas. B) Help remove pandas from the list of endangered species. C) Shed light on the conservation of most large meat-eating animals. D) Show the complexity of interactions between humans and animals.

【选项】A) 以偏概全 Sillero 的话恰恰是说"超出熊猫保护"，Help discover new ways for the conservation of pandas. 把启示范围又拉回熊猫，与原文方向相反。 B) 张冠李戴 putting them on the list of vulnerable, but not endangered, species 只是说现状已 不在 endangered 名单，并非新发现的功效。Help remove pandas from the list of endangered species. 把背景数据当作新发现的功效。 C) ✓ 正确 implications beyond panda conservation ↔ Shed light on the conservation of most large meat-eating animals. Most large animals that eat meat live in increasingly fragmented landscapes ↔ most large meat-eating animals C 用 Shed light on + most large meat-eating animals 直接对应原文 implications beyond panda conservation + Most large animals that eat meat，与预判完全 一致。 D) 偷换概念 Sillero 强调 induces more animals to scatter or travel further，给出的是积极效益， 不是 Show the complexity of interactions between humans and animals. 那种中 性"展示复杂性"。
